The PR changes (dependabot dependency bumps) are completely unrelated to this failure # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information - **Prow Job**: pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-aks - **Build ID**: 2074105729261768704 - **Target**: e2e-aks - **Failed Test**: `TestAzureScheduler/ValidateHostedCluster/EnsureNoCrashingPods` - **PR**: [#8849](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8849) — NO-JIRA: chore(deps): weekly dependabot consolidation ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` Container openshift-oauth-apiserver in pod openshift-oauth-apiserver-66b8fdb877-vr549 has a restartCount > 0 (1) ``` ### Summary The `TestAzureScheduler` test failed because the `EnsureNoCrashingPods` validation detected that the `openshift-oauth-apiserver` container in the hosted control plane namespace had restarted once (`restartCount=1`). The container crashed on its first startup attempt because it could not establish a connection to etcd (`etcd-client:2379`) — first DNS resolution failed, then TCP connections timed out. After 20 seconds the container exited with `"error building REST storage: context deadline exceeded"` (exit code 1). It restarted successfully and remained healthy. This is a transient hosted control plane startup race condition unrelated to the PR's dependabot dependency bumps. All other tests in this same job run (22 other `EnsureNoCrashingPods` checks) passed.
Root Cause The `openshift-oauth-apiserver` container in pod `openshift-oauth-apiserver-66b8fdb877-vr549` (hosted control plane namespace `e2e-clusters-dcd6v-azure-scheduler-rfhbf`) crashed during its initial startup at `13:01:23Z` due to an etcd connectivity race condition: 1. **DNS resolution failure** — At `13:01:23Z`, the container tried to connect to `etcd-client:2379` but DNS lookup failed: `"dial tcp: lookup etcd-client: operation was canceled"` 2. **TCP connection timeouts** — At `13:01:43Z` (20 seconds later), subsequent connection attempts to the resolved IP `10.0.68.198:2379` were also canceled 3. **Context deadline exceeded** — At `13:01:43Z`, the container gave up with: `"error building REST storage: context deadline exceeded"` and exited with code 1 4. **Successful restart** — The container restarted at `13:01:44Z` and became healthy, running without further issues The `EnsureNoCrashingPods` test function (in `test/e2e/util/util.go`) checks all pods in the hosted control plane namespace and fails if any container has `restartCount > crashToleration`. For the Azure platform (non-Kubevirt), `defaultCrashToleration = 0`, and `openshift-oauth-apiserver` is not in the `podCrashTolerations` exception map. Therefore, a single restart (`restartCount=1 > 0`) caused the test to fail. This is a **known pattern of transient startup races** in hosted control planes where the oauth-apiserver starts before etcd DNS is fully resolvable. The dependabot changes in PR #8849 (Go version bump 1.25.7→1.25.8, AWS SDK update, KubeVirt CRD doc changes) have no relationship to etcd connectivity or oauth-apiserver startup.
Recommendations 1. **Retrigger the job** — This is a transient infrastructure-level startup race, not a code regression. Run `/test e2e-aks` to retrigger. 2. **Consider adding `openshift-oauth-apiserver` to `podCrashTolerations`** — Similar to the existing tolerations for `ingress-operator` (20 restarts), `dns-operator` (5 restarts), and `network-node-identity` (1 restart), adding a toleration of 1 restart for `openshift-oauth-apiserver` would prevent this known transient startup race from causing flaky test failures. The etcd DNS resolution race during HCP startup is analogous to the leader election and startup timing issues already tolerated for other components. 3. **File a tracking issue** — If not already tracked, consider filing a bug to investigate whether the oauth-apiserver startup can be made more resilient to etcd DNS resolution delays (e.g., longer initial backoff, readiness gate on etcd availability).
